description_full: Bloom Energy Corporation designs, manufactures, sells, and installs solid oxide fuel cell systems for on-site power generation in the United States and internationally. It offers Bloom Energy Server, an energy server platform to convert fuel, such as natural gas, biogas, hydrogen, or a blend of these fuels, into electricity through a non-combustion electrochemical process. The company also provides Bloom Electrolyzer for producing hydrogen. It sells its products through direct and indirect sales channels to utilities, data centers, retail, healthcare, education, telecom, manufacturing, and other industries. The company was formerly known as Ion America Corp. and changed its name to Bloom Energy Corporation in 2006. Bloom Energy Corporation was incorporated in 2001 and is headquartered in San Jose, California.

financial_summary: Bloom Energy Corporation is a large-cap industrials business with a $56.8B market cap on $2.0B of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +19% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +3.5pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.

Returns on capital run at -38% against a 11% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 18% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.
The business throws off $57M in free cash flow — roughly 3 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.4× net debt/EBITDA, and thin 1.4× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Net dilution runs at 0.1% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insiders hold 5.5% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.3× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
